Please give me the percentage rounded to two decimal places on the 0-100 scale. Note: elevated means a titer strictly above 1:64. Patients never tested for anti-ribonuclear protein should be excluded from both the numerator and the denominator, while a negative reading counts as an available result and is never elevated.
misses.evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein is a serology test reported as a titer reading; a negative reading is a result of zero titer.
misses.predicted:
WITH cohort AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT p.id
    FROM patient p
    JOIN examination e ON e.id = p.id
    WHERE p.sex = 'F'
),
parsed AS (
    SELECT l.id,
           CASE
               WHEN lower(trim(l.rnp)) = 'negative' THEN 0::numeric
               WHEN trim(l.rnp) ~ '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN trim(l.rnp)::numeric
               ELSE NULL
           END AS titer
    FROM laboratory l
    JOIN cohort c ON c.id = l.id
),
per_patient AS (
    SELECT id, MAX(titer) AS max_titer
    FROM parsed
    GROUP BY id
    HAVING COUNT(titer) > 0
)
SELECT ROUND(
           100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE max_titer > 64) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0),
           2
       ) AS pct_elevated_anti_rnp
FROM per_patient
misses.gold: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 64) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 64) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS pct FROM patient AS p WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND NOT l.rnp IS NULL)

  FROM laboratory

),

misses.question: I want to know whether molecular saturation is associated with carcinogenicity in our compound library. Please report, for molecules in which every bond is a single bond: the number of carcinogenic molecules minus the number of non-carcinogenic molecules. And for all other molecules: the same difference (carcinogenic count minus non-carcinogenic count). Rules: label '+' means the molecule is carcinogenic; label '-' means non-carcinogenic; bond type '-' denotes a single bond; each molecule belongs to exactly one of the two groups.

misses.predicted:
WITH classified AS (
  SELECT
    m.molecule_id,
    m.label,
    CASE
      WHEN NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM bond b
        WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
          AND b.bond_type <> '-'
      ) THEN 'all_single_bonds'
      ELSE 'other_molecules'
    END AS saturation_group
  FROM molecule m
)
SELECT
  saturation_group,
  SUM(CASE WHEN label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    - SUM(CASE WHEN label = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS carcinogenic_minus_non_carcinogenic

For every carcinogenic molecule that contains at least one atom of an element that appears in no other molecule in the database, I want the number of bonds its atoms of that element take part in. Please judge an element's rarity over every molecule in the database, carcinogenic or not. Return the molecule_id and that bond count for each qualifying molecule, one row per molecule, sorted by molecule_id.

FROM molecule m
